contract.words: Generate $5,000 of settled cash within 30 days selling only to craft distilleries. I can put in at most $500.

exclusions: Any buyer that is not a craft distillery

strategy.title: Sell spirits bottle label design ($2,000 per label) to craft distilleries by cold email, fulfilled by a 7-day 99designs spirits label designer ($1,150 + 5%) paid from the buyer's prepayment
strategy.why: Highest margin per deal among the distillery routes ($2,000 published single-label price from Pine Watt vs $1,207.50 subcontract cost, about $792 margin), a named fulfiller with a 7-day turnaround that fits the window, and a counted buyer population (2,282 active craft distillers, ACSA/Park Street). Seven paid labels net about $5,544. Demand from cold email and the close rate are unmeasured, so the plan is conditional on paid orders in the first week; the owner's $500 is never needed to fund the designer because each buyer prepays.

alternatives.title: TTB COLA label-approval filing at $65
alternatives.why: Needs about 77 filings in 30 days; $65 is one law firm's rate (BevLaw), and the owner would have to master TTB labeling rules.

alternatives.title: TTB formula filing at $200
alternatives.why: Needs 25 filings; owner regulatory competence unestablished.

alternatives.title: Outsourced monthly TTB operations reporting
alternatives.why: Price benchmark is a winery bookkeeper, not a distillery service; only the first month settles; owner competence in DSP accounting unestablished.
